method: Fresh verifier sub-agent and independent adversarial falsifier sub-agent run in parallel per policy/verification.md §5. Announcement claim type for the term-sheet/valuation/use-of-funds facts (Tier-0 primary source: Databricks' own press release); business claim type for the $3B raise amount (wire-exclusive check applied, per §2).
origin_items: Surfaced via this cycle's discovery sweep (recurring query 'AI company funding round announcement'), not from the feed ingest. dedup-check before opening: clean, no matches.

claims.text: Databricks signed a term sheet for a strategic funding round valuing the company at $188 billion, led by existing investor Coatue Management, expected to close later summer 2026
claims.reasoning: Confirmed directly by Databricks' own newsroom press release (Tier-0 primary source), corroborated by Reuters' own wire text (via Yahoo Finance syndication) and TechCrunch's named-byline reporting (Julie Bort). Falsifier specifically checked whether 'signed' overstates 'in talks'/'seeking' framing used by some outlets (e.g. a Yahoo headline saying 'Seeks') and found Databricks' own release states plainly it has signed a term sheet, consistent with 'expected to close later this summer' -- not overstated.

claims.text: The round is reported to include a $3 billion investment, per Wall Street Journal sourcing citing people familiar with the matter -- a figure Databricks has not itself confirmed
claims.reasoning: Wire-exclusive check run per §2: every outlet found (Reuters, TechCrunch, Yahoo, US News, SiliconANGLE, Investing.com) traces the $3B figure to the same WSJ report citing anonymous sources; none add independent confirmation. Databricks' own release does not disclose an amount. Note: TechCrunch/Reuters phrase the non-response as Coatue 'could not immediately be reached for comment' rather than an affirmative decline -- the published article avoids the stronger 'declined to comment' wording the falsifier flagged as unsupported.

claims.text: The $188 billion valuation is roughly a 40% increase from the $134 billion valuation Databricks reached in February 2026, when it raised about $5 billion
claims.reasoning: Independently stated by both Reuters (via Yahoo Finance) and TechCrunch as established background (TechCrunch dates the prior round to February 2026, consistent with CNBC's Feb 9 2026 report the falsifier located separately). Math checks: 188/134 ≈ 1.403, a ~40% increase. No date conflation with the new round found.

claims.text: Databricks said the new capital will fund expansion of its Unity AI Gateway, Genie AI assistant and Lakebase database products, plus potential future AI acquisitions
claims.reasoning: Directly stated in Databricks' own press release, naming all three products and future AI acquisitions/research as intended uses of the capital.

falsifier_notes: Overall verdict: CLEAR TO PUBLISH. No dispute, denial, or retraction found for the $188B figure or the deal itself across any outlet searched, including pieces dated as late as 19 July. No conflation between this round and the earlier Feb 2026 $134B/$5B round -- confirmed as genuinely separate events. One wording nuance caught and corrected before publication: 'Coatue declined to comment' would have overstated sourcing that actually says Coatue 'could not immediately be reached for comment'; the published article omits the comment detail entirely rather than risk the inaccurate framing. Databricks Newsroom is an unregistered Tier-0 source -- proposed for registration in source_candidates.json.
